subject.title: Control UI fails to load on Firefox desktop behind reverse proxy — CSP blocks Vite runtime eval(), 'Control UI did not start', WebSocket 1006

question: Should maintainers keep this issue separate for Firefox reverse-proxy/WebSocket proof, or fold it into the existing Control UI CSP/Zod issue and treat the socket failure as blocked-startup fallout?
rationale: The CSP/root-cause evidence overlaps an open security-sensitive issue, but this report adds a reverse-proxy socket failure that may need live browser/proxy proof before gateway behavior changes.

options.title: Keep Separate Pending Live Proof
options.body: Track the reverse-proxy WebSocket failure here while the strict-CSP no-eval fix remains tied to the existing CSP issue.

options.title: Fold Into CSP Thread
options.body: Close this as a duplicate if maintainers accept the socket failure as a consequence of the same blocked Control UI bundle startup.

options.title: Fix CSP First, Then Re-Test
options.body: Prioritize the no-eval Control UI fix under the existing CSP issue and request fresh reverse-proxy diagnostics only if startup still fails.

recommendation.title: Keep Separate Pending Live Proof
recommendation.body: Track the reverse-proxy WebSocket failure here while the strict-CSP no-eval fix remains tied to the existing CSP issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest history signal across Control UI CSP, Gateway serving, and browser connection/auth behavior.
